What We Learned at Web Summit 2019

Published November 12, 2019 by Sarah Chen

Last week our team returned from Web Summit 2019 in Lisbon with pages of notes, too many photos, and a much clearer picture of where digital experience platforms were heading. This recap captures the main ideas that stood out to us at the time, especially around privacy, analytics, and product-led growth.

Privacy moved from niche concern to board-level topic

Several speakers framed privacy as one of the defining commercial questions for 2020. The strongest sessions focused on first-party data strategies, consent design, and the growing expectation that brands should earn trust instead of assuming it.

Analytics teams expected a major transition in 2020

One of the most repeated themes at this year's event was that analytics and attribution models would need to evolve rapidly before the end of 2020. Sessions on measurement pointed to looming browser restrictions, reduced signal access, and heavier pressure on owned data collection.

Three practical takeaways we brought home

  • Build stronger first-party data habits before disruption forces the change.
  • Reduce friction between editorial, product, and analytics teams.
  • Treat trust signals as part of the product experience, not only a legal requirement.

We will be using these lessons to shape Meridian's client workshops through the rest of this year and into 2020.
